## 70c1f7fc5056

**A2 — Reproduced documentation/authority mismatch and ignored controls.** Current generator v2.0.2 has SHA-256 881c307c04c4ef53b240a33e08082948d27254450d49a92db52bbf9db9d7c56b. The description says to discard the original prototype and stamp only at color9 anchors. The actual canonical Racket initializes output by pasting the original prototype, then adds each anchor stamp. An independent retain-prototype oracle matches all5 saved canonical pairs; the advertised discard formulation matches0/5. All120 sampled inputs across default/easy/hard pass self_check and distinguish those two formulations. The retained generated witness was then executed by canonical Racket: it is in domain, preserves the original prototype and disagrees with the advertised discard output. This is a description defect; generated labels already use the canonical authority, so no incorrect produced label is claimed.

The same seeded draw is byte-for-byte unchanged for palette_kind=warm versus cool, and also for invalid palette_kind, invalid texture and an unknown override name. All five controls are silently accepted. Source inspection confirms that ordinary palette/texture values are not consumed; only degenerate texture names branch. This undermines the advertised parameter controls. No core semantic contract is declared, so demonstration sufficiency remains unknown. The 120-input sample does not establish exhaustive generation correctness.

Evidence: checks/audit/70c1f7fc5056/probe.py, report.json and witness.json; canonical application in racket.json; the explicit comparison in racket-verification.json. Exact commands and exits are in checks/commands/audit-70c1f7fc5056-python.log, audit-70c1f7fc5056-racket.log and verify-final-labels.log. Suggested repair is to align documentation with the retained-prototype rule, implement or remove the unused declared axes, reject unsupported values/names, and add a finite teaching contract. No source, Racket, approval or resolution was changed for this audit.
